answer: Because the pigment index resolves every citation against the sparrow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the willow audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 182 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 182 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
